name: Esenboğa International Airport
before:
Ankara's airport, 28 km north east of the Turkish capital, and fourth busiest in the country after the two Istanbul airports and Antalya. It carried more than 13 million passengers in 2025, ten million of them domestic, which tells you what this airport is for.

It has a good record. ACI Europe named it the best airport in Europe in its size category in 2009, the first such award to a Turkish airport, singling out an unusual piece of environmental engineering: the terminal recycles exhaust gases to power its air conditioning, saving about 25 per cent of its energy. ACI gave it a second award in 2020 in the 15 to 25 million category.

The terminal opened in October 2006 under a build, operate and transfer contract, and a separate general aviation terminal for private aircraft followed in January 2012.

A second parallel runway is under construction to the east, and the runway designations will change when it opens.

The name comes from the village of Esenboğa, from Isen Buqa, a Turkic commander in Timur's army who settled his troops here at the Battle of Ankara in 1402.
after:
Ankara's airport, 28 km north east of the Turkish capital and fourth busiest in the country after the two Istanbul airports and Antalya. It carried almost 14 million passengers in 2025, ten million of them domestic, which tells you what this airport is for.

ACI Europe once named it the best airport in Europe in the 5 to 10 million passenger category.

The terminal opened in 2006, and a separate general aviation terminal for private aircraft followed.

TAV Airports, which runs the airport, says a second runway, 3,750 metres long, has now been completed.

The name comes from the village of Esenboğa, from Isen Buqa, a Turkic commander in Timur's army who made camp here at the Battle of Ankara in 1402.

claims.note: Eurostat's 2025 table of passengers carried covers all 872 airports that report to it, 58 of them Turkish. Its values are indexed by (airport x 4 + schedule) x 7 + coverage, so an airport's total (schedule and coverage both TOTAL, index 0) sits at its airport index x 28. claims.claim: the name comes from the village of Esenboga, from Isen Buqa, a Turkic commander in Timur's army at the Battle of Ankara in 1402, who camped here
claims.inAfter: The name comes from the village of Esenboğa, from Isen Buqa, a Turkic commander in Timur's army who made camp here at the Battle of Ankara in 1402.
claims.note: Was 'who settled his troops here'. Hurriyet's column (in Turkish) says Esenboga is a person's name, originally Isen Buga, one of Timur's generals and a ruler of the Chagatai state, one of the Turkic empires of Asia; that he fought in the 1402 battle at Ankara, near Cubuk, and set up his headquarters at the place now named after him, Esenboga being the worn-down form of his name; and that the airfield was built at the small settlement called Esenboga and given its name. 'Made camp' is the plain common ground of 'set up his headquarters' and Wikipedia's 'settled his troops'.

‘‘Esenboğa’’ denilen küçük yerleşim merkezinin bulunduğu yerde... İnşaat tamamlandı ve alana bulunduğu yerin adı verildi.

sources.quote: The name of the airport comes from the village of Esenboğa, which literally means "Windflowing Bull" or "Serene Bull", the modernized form of Isen Buqa, the name of a Turkic warlord in the army of Timur who settled his troops here during the Battle of Ankara in 1402.

claims.claim: a second ACI award in 2020, in the 15 to 25 million category
claims.wasBefore: ACI gave it a second award in 2020 in the 15 to 25 million category.
claims.why: Good sources disagree. Wikipedia says ACI named it best European airport of 15 to 25 million passengers in 2020; TAV's 2023 brochure for the airport says 'Best airport in Europe 2019', rewarded by ACI Europe, with no category; and TAV's own figures put 2019 traffic at about 13.7 million (11.46 million domestic, 2.28 million international), below that band. ACI's 2020 release could not be reached (404 at the address Wikipedia cites, and a news index at the same path without /news/), and ACI's list of past winners starts at 2021. Cut rather than pick a year or category. The quotes below show the disagreement; the brochure's text is saved with the PDF's broken 'i' glyphs.
